title: Growth Stalls Ahead of Forecast
summary: Payrolls, orders, and freight volumes all turned down together; the slowdown is broader than the transition briefings assumed.
briefing_text: Three of the four leading indicators the Council tracks moved down last month, and the fourth is flat. Manufacturing orders have fallen for a second consecutive month and rail freight loadings are at their weakest level in three years. Treasury judges this a genuine deceleration rather than statistical noise, but the Council is split on whether it becomes a contraction. You have perhaps one quarter before the answer is decided for you.

cabinet_assessment.state: Our trading partners are slowing with us, Mr. President, which limits how much export demand can rescue the quarter. If we act, a coordinated announcement with allied finance ministries would be worth more than acting alone a week earlier.
cabinet_assessment.defense: I have no view on the monetary question, sir, but I will tell you that a stimulus of any size will be paid for out of the outyear defense topline. That is where these bills always land.
cabinet_assessment.treasury: This is a demand-side slowdown, not a supply shock, and it is shallow so far. Anything we do should be temporary, targeted, and reversible; permanent commitments made in a soft quarter are how deficits become structural.
cabinet_assessment.nsa: Economic weakness narrows every option I bring you on the foreign side. Adversaries read a distracted Washington accurately and price it into their own risk-taking.
cabinet_assessment.chief_of_staff: You have four months before this becomes the only thing anyone asks you about. Acting now is a choice; being seen to act in June is not a choice, it is damage control.
cabinet_assessment.intelligence: Our reporting on external demand is moderate confidence at best, sir. What I can say is that two of our major partners are revising their own forecasts downward and have not announced it yet.

choices.label: Emergency Stimulus Package
choices.description: Send Congress a broad spending and transfer package designed to reach households within a quarter.

advisor_positions.treasury: It will work, Mr. President, and it will cost more than the number on the cover. Size it for the slowdown we have, not the one we fear.
advisor_positions.chief_of_staff: This is the option people will feel. It is also the option that hands the opposition a deficit number to run on for two years.
advisor_positions.defense: Understand that this crowds out the procurement request I am bringing you in the spring, sir.

choices.outcome_text: The package cleared both chambers on a narrow, bruising vote. Treasury expects the transfers to reach households inside a quarter; the deficit line moved by more than the White House wanted printed.

advisor_positions.treasury: This is the option I can defend line by line, Mr. President. It is smaller than the moment may seem to demand, and that is deliberate.
advisor_positions.chief_of_staff: It passes. That is its virtue. Nobody writes a song about it either.

choices.outcome_text: The relief bill passed comfortably and cost less than half of what the Council had modelled. Whether it is enough depends on a quarter of data nobody has yet.

choices.label: Hold the Line on Spending
choices.description: Decline new fiscal measures, defend the deficit path, and let automatic stabilizers do the work.

advisor_positions.treasury: It is the disciplined answer, Mr. President, and discipline is only a virtue if the slowdown stays shallow. If it does not, we will be acting later from a weaker position.
advisor_positions.chief_of_staff: If unemployment prints above five and a half before the summer, this decision will be replayed in every advertisement you see for two years.

memory.action: declined fiscal support as the slowdown deepened
memory.result: unemployment rose; restraint became a liability

advisor_positions.treasury: I can arrange the meeting, Mr. President. I would ask you to be careful with the language afterward, because independence is easier to spend than to rebuild.
advisor_positions.intelligence: Foreign services read our institutional friction closely, sir. A joint statement will be studied for signs of pressure whether or not any exists.
